questions.stem:
Statements:
Some cats are animals.
All animals are living.
Only a few living are dogs.

Conclusions:
I. No cats being dogs is a possibility.
II. No animals are dogs.

In each of the questions below, some statements are given followed by two conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.
options: If either I or II follows
If neither I nor II follows
If both I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (a) If only I follows

The cats–animal overlap can avoid the dog subset of living, so no cats being dogs is possible (I). Nothing states that all animals avoid dogs; II is not a necessary conclusion.

questions.stem:

No pages are cover.
Some cover is white.

Conclusions:
I. Some white is not pages.
II. No books are cover.

In each of the questions below, some statements are given followed by two conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.
options: If either I or II follows
If neither I nor II follows
If both I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (e) If both I and II follow

Some covers are white and no cover is a page, so some white objects are not pages (I). Books are pages, and no page is a cover; hence no book is a cover (II). Both follow.

questions.stem:
What is the code for “rain” in the given code language?

Study the following information carefully and answer the question.
In a certain code language:
“Rain plain sky cloud” is coded as “sf gi yt cn”
“Cloud cricket ball Pencil” is coded as “te ku fa cn”
“Lawn cricket plain home” is coded as “fa je gi ho”
“Sky lawn park” is coded as “yt ho dw”
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (a) sf

Compare the repeated words across the given sentences. A word and its code occur in the same sentences. This gives:

ball → ku or te
cloud → cn
cricket → fa
home → je
lawn → ho
park → dw
pencil → ku or te
plain → gi
rain → sf
sky → yt

Where two words share the same possible codes, their individual codes cannot be distinguished without an additional clue. Apply any extra code given in this question before selecting the answer.

questions.stem:
In which direction is point F with respect to point B?
Read the given information carefully and answer the questions based on it:
Rahul starts from point A and walks 10 meters towards the North to reach point B. From point B, he takes a right
turn and walks 15 meters to reach point C. At point C, he takes another right turn and walks 20 meters to reach
point D. From D, he then makes a 90 - degree turn to the left and walks 5 meters to reach point E. Finally, from E,
he takes a left turn and walks 25 meters to reach point F .
questions.explanation:
Source answer: (a) North-east

Take east as positive x and north as positive y. Apply each turn or positional clue to obtain:

A (0,0), B (0,10), C (15,10), D (15,−10), E (20,−10), F (20,15).

F is 20 m east and 5 m north of B, so it is north-east of B.

Take east as positive x and north as positive y. Apply each turn or positional clue to obtain:

A (0,0), B (0,10), C (15,10), D (15,−10), E (20,−10), F (20,15).
